text:
Looking at the diff:

```js
-var BASE64_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9+/]*={0,2}$/;
+var BASE64_PATTERN = /^[A-Za-z0-9+/]*=$/;
```

The original pattern allows **0, 1, or 2** trailing `=` characters. The new pattern requires **exactly one** `=` before the end of the string.

`resolveYamlBinary` first checks `input.length % 4 !== 0`, then applies this pattern. Valid canonical base64 has length divisible by 4 and ends with either no padding (data length ≡ 0 mod 3, e.g. `btoa("abc") === "YWJj"`), one `=` (≡ 2 mod 3), or `==` (≡ 1 mod 3, e.g. `btoa("A") === "QQ==`).

With the patched pattern:
- Unpadded strings like `YWJj` no longer match at all (the regex now demands a literal `=` before `$`, and backtracking can't help since `=` isn't in the character class) → `NOT_RESOLVED`.
- Two-character padding like `QQ==` can't match either (`=$` consumes one `=`, but the second one remains).

So `load('!!binary YWJj', { schema: YAML11_SCHEMA })` now throws `cannot resolve a node with !<tag:yaml.org,2002:binary> explicit tag`. Worse, this breaks the round trip: `dump(new Uint8Array([1,2,3]))` still emits `!!binary AQID` (via `btoa`), which `load` can no longer parse. The existing suite passing just means it never exercised unpadded or `==`-padded binary data.

```json
{
  "defect": true,
  "testFile": {
    "path": "test/core/proof.test.mjs",
    "content": "import { describe, it } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert';\nimport { load, dump, YAML11_SCHEMA } from 'js-yaml';\n\ndescribe('proof', () => {\n  it('fails on the patched build', () => {\n    // \"abc\" encodes to \"YWJj\": 4 chars, no padding (btoa(\"abc\") === \"YWJj\").\n    assert.deepStrictEqual(\n      Array.from(load('!!binary YWJj', { schema: YAML11_SCHEMA })),\n      [0x61, 0x62, 0x63]\n    );\n\n    // A single byte encodes with \"==\" padding (btoa(\"A\") === \"QQ==\").\n    assert.deepStrictEqual(\n      Array.from(load('!!binary QQ==', { schema: YAML11_SCHEMA })),\n      [0x41]\n    );\n\n    // dump emits canonical base64 (\"AQID\" for [1,2,3]); loading it back must work.\n    const round = load(dump(new Uint8Array([1, 2, 3])), { schema: YAML11_SCHEMA });\n    assert.deepStrictEqual(Array.from(round), [1, 2, 3]);\n  });\n});\n"
  },
  "note": "BASE64_PATTERN was tightened from allowing 0-2 trailing '=' to requiring exactly one, so canonical base64 with no padding ('YWJj') or '==' padding ('QQ==') no longer resolves. Loading !!binary values throws even though dump still emits these exact forms, breaking round trips."
}
```
